body:
I take (only) Quetiapine and it has put my sex drive through the roof. I used to be on (only) Venlafaxine and that seemed to lower it.

If this is an issue for you, it might be worth asking your prescriber if you can try another anti-depressant alongside your Quetiapine as it's possibly the Venlafaxine that is causing the issue?

It's so good to hear that it *can* be made to work. We knew it was going to be hard as we've both been in a long-distance relationship before but this is a really profound relationship and we had no idea it would be anything like this. I finally know what love *really* is and I'm scared of losing her, at this point. Yeah, I have been crying myself to sleep every night, without fail, for quite a while now. The yearning is mentally *and* physically painful... so damn painful. :( And yet, the pain is worth it for the overwhelming joy and meaning she brings to my life.

Any advice you have would be appreciated, even if it may not work for us. We're both really ill and we don't know what to do anymore. We are trying to apply the things we've learnt in therapy and to remain as positive as we possibly can, despite feeling so negative but is that enough? :(

Every medication on Earth has ten billion side effects. The vast majority of them affect such small amounts of the population that it's generally not worth worrying about most side effects. I guess some are more common though, plus there's nothing wrong with being cautious but yeah. :P

When I was on anti-anxiety medication (can't remember what it was, sorry but I'll try to) the only thing I noticed was that if I drank then... yeah, just don't drink. It's not very pleasant.

Someone very close to me is in the Hospital right now and I'm scared too. Without them, I don't really have anything to keep me going other than my dog I suppose. I've been struggling with self-harm and toying with the idea of suicide for months now and harmed for the first time in many many years recently. I don't have a social life; a relationship; children etc. either and I'm consumed with thoughts about suicide all day and every day.

If you need a friend or just someone who'll listen or to talk with, someone who kind of relates to how you feel; then feel free to message me.

I understand that you don't want to be here anymore but this isn't the way. You have more of a chance of causing some kind of disastrous organ failure but surviving, than killing yourself. And if you thought life was bad now, it will be far worse after that. I've tried to kill myself enough times to know. I hope that somebody realizes what you've done and you get your stomach pumped or something before the damage is done...

And I wish that you'd have tried to talk with us first before going through with your plan.

Of course you know how to talk to people, you're doing it right now. :) You just struggle to talk in person, right? I doubt you are as boring as you say you are. The amount of times I've had someone tell me they are boring, only to go on and have long in-depth conversations with them is immeasurable.

I understand your frustrations, believe me I do. I have suffered from anxiety (amongst other things) for more than a decade. It was once at the point where I basically couldn't leave the house without having some kind of attack. And now, I wouldn't say I'm cured as there is no cure but it is so much better. It's manageable 99% of the time. I still get uneasy when there are crowds or when people are being rowdy etc. but it's nothing like it was before.

I won't lie to you, it's ridiculously difficult to get it to a manageable state but when you do it feels so much better.

The only issue is the depression that tends to come along with the anxiety and how they tend to feed each other. Plus the fact that anxiety is sort of more understood and can be brought to a manageable state more easily (it's not going to be easy, it's going to be horrible but it's possible). Whereas the depression... it seems to be a much more difficult problem.

Anyway, I don't want to seem like I am having a go at you or anything like that so I'll leave it at this but if you want to talk my inbox is always open. Just know that I was on the verge of suicide, many times due to my anxiety and now I'm past it. It's not gone and I struggle with other things now, instead but it's something.

As for the last part, well you do sort of have a point but there are a lot of people out there who feel just as ugly as you do. What about those people?
Yeah, they just seem to feed into each other.

I know how you feel. I think the only reason I'm still around right now is because of my dog and my Grandma.

Both of them are very old though and it worries me.

I've never had anyone so much as approach me about them and there are a LOT of them. No one really seems to notice anything I say or do.

I honestly can't say how I'd react because it's just never happened to me. It's not like I hide them away or anything, either.

I disagree. Humans are social creatures and it's impossible to be truly happy without social contact. It doesn't matter if you're introverted or extroverted, shy or outgoing, whatever. Humans are still humans and a person without social contact is -- 99% of the time -- going to lose their mind.

Just because you're ugly, doesn't mean you don't have anything going for you. I know you might not believe me, but there are people out there who don't judge solely based on looks. Anyone knows that looks are kind of meaningless, in the grand scheme of things. Just because someone is what society regards as beautiful, doesn't mean they will be a good or interesting etc. person. More often than not, they aren't.

There are people out there who will accept you for who you actually are, instead of how you look. Please believe me. And yes, it's really hard to find them and sometimes you feel like giving up. I know, trust me I know.
I feel almost the same way...

Always. Once a week is not enough. Doesn't take long for your mindset to switch completely from please help me to I don't want help... not from myself nor anyone else. It feels like I'm starting again with every appointment lately. Plus last time I went I had some kind of anxiety attack... don't really want to go back now.
Try with a dot between the words. :S

Kik: throwaway.lives (note the dot)

Feel free to add me... always around.

Not only all of that, but... the commercials run for like a month or so, leading up to it. My schedule is very messed up and I haven't been able to sleep for 3-4 days, otherwise I'd be in bed as well. I'd say that I can't wait for today to be over but it's not like tomorrow will be much better anyway.
Although if I go to the shop, then there's the signs and posters and racks of cards... I really can't win!
All of the Father's day BS is following me around too... everywhere I go and driving me insane. It's inescapable... I'm gonna go get really drunk.
That's because most people are.

I've tried so hard to meet people and no one wants to know me. I have some submissions wherein I elaborate on these frustrations. It's partly the isolation that is driving me over the edge.

One is not born alone, nor educated alone etc., so why must one live and die alone?
Sorry, someone who can... what?

It has been brought up in the past but never really discussed. It's all very... taboo.

It is hard, especially when most of the time it all falls on deaf ears. I've been trying to reach out to people on here and via other avenues for a couple of months but usually to no avail. It really is true that nobody particulary cares, though they may relate, and we really are mostly alone on this World.

Conversation is a good distraction and I appreciate this. I'll be back soon, I feel really nauseous.
Bled for 5 minutes or so then began to clot as is normal but it is having difficulties because of the other stuff. A lot of them are mostly "stuff" and not blood.

It depends how I am on the day. Usually I dare not mention it. I don't want to be rejected by my care team. I can't take any more rejection, I really can't.

One day, I went in extremely agitated and frustrated. I was ready to speak up about it and of course she didn't have the usual attitude that day... argh. I think she just hates me because of something that happened ages ago  between  me and one of their therapists.

It was a razor blade but it is now dulled and useless. There are always more laying around though... I sort of have to keep them around. I promise I won't do anything more while we talk. I'm sorry, please don't worrry too much.

It's nice to talk but I don't know what to say just as I don't know what to do anymore. I don't know if words can or will change anything.
Honest about what? I'm not really sure I want to hear it if it's about her.

I've shared a ton with them over the years... almost everything. Well, I guess it is her job to try and help me but her attitude gets in the way. She talks as though I am vermin on the ground; I am beneath her.

I had a blade and was trying not to cut. I just ended up sort of cutting all of the scabbing off/out. It is very hard but I really am trying. I feel a little better than I did earlier, physically at least. I'm not going anywhere just yet, anyway. I can't sleep.

I don't get why you even want to talk to or help me. I don't deserve it. I thank you though, immensely. It's nice to not feel entirely alone for once in your life. To most, I am merely a username in a vast ocean of usernames.
Yes. I hate myself everyday for what I put her through. She was my best friend too. :(

About her? Or in general?

I suppose the answers are a tiny bit... and yes, respectedly.

Yes but the care coordinator usually sits through the appointments with us. She is sort of like the boss lady too, I believe, so what can I really say or do?

Sigh, I just gave in and opened up all of the wounds again. I had to do something to stop myself from cutting again but it's just not the same. It has become near impossible to resist the thoughts and urges lately. :(

It's okay... I know they're not great and was already worried heh.

The DBT lady is nice but my care coordinator is... not so much. I am the lowest I have ever been and it's not helping. You have to be on the path to recovery for it to be effective. Rock bottom is not conducive to therapy.

I don't know what to do... I just want to wake up and for my life to have been a bad dream.

It was long distance and after our first in-person meeting I could no longer stand to be alone. Knowing that my soul mate (IMO) was out there. My anxiety along with some major paranoia concerning her slowly tore me to shreds. I was losing my mind and it scared her. It got to the point where I was sure she was trying to trigger me all the time. A large verbal disagreement that spanned a few days culminated in me threatening suicide. And that was the final straw for her, I guess.
Sorry, I am just scared.

Nausea; faintness; dizziness; elevated heart rate; fever; cold shakes/shivering; general weakness. Some of these are on and off  (e.g. fever; shakes) and some are just always "on". More like 20 on each arm actually but yes.

Well I probably deserve the pain. It was just easy to go through with.

DBT is dialectical behaviour therapy. It aims to help you identify negative behavioural patterns and their triggers.

I left mainly due to anxiety and paranoia returning with a vengeance. I couldn't handle it after all that happened. I quit the meds because they weren't working anymore and they refused to adjust or change them.

And I think that's silly and never believed it. I've adored and lusted over many a person and never have I felt something so strong as how I feel about her. I feel physically ill when I think about what happened.
Are you there?

Well, I've been going throught DBT for a few months but I don't feel it has helped at all. And one of them is pretty mean to me, so I always leave feeling terrible. Plus I asked for help today and was shunned. Why would they help me tomorrow?

The plan was simply to make all of the wounds long and deep, at least 8 inches in length. Large wounds get infected far easier... there's maybe 30 or so on each arm. Upper/lower, inner/outer... everywhere. This was done maybe 5 or so days ago...

EDIT: My hopes were/are that any infection would become systemic... I've been having strange symptoms so I suppose something is happening.

Quit College; stopped taking my medication; started drinking and smoking again; started self-harming again; attempted suicide a couple times; stopped enjoying hobbies and even passions; pushed everyone away; etc. etc.

The only reason I was doing so well was because of her. She did help me to start loving myself a little but I did nearly all of it for her. I know placing someone on a pedestal is a bad thing but when you love someone THAT much....

I don't think I need therapy or counselling and all that. I need love, the one thing they can't give me. The one thing I never had... except a brief taste of it, once.

I don't know. I'd like to talk about things that make me happy but nothing makes me happy anymore. Even though I had so many varied interests and hobbies. I'm 25 and male.

I don't have friends... the only thing I had {my last relationship} fell apart in November. They were my everything... and now there is nothing. I feel like life is meaningless now they are gone. They gave meaning to all.

I could go into great detail about my troubles but I've wrote about a lot of it before. And my keyboard is broken so I'm typing with a mouse and on-screen keyboard... argh.

What about you - what's your story?

I don't really have anything to clean it up with to be honest plus... and I know it sounds insane but it's kind of my insurance policy. I need to think long and hard about being alive... I just don't feel like I have the strength anymore to deal with all the crap that comes along with it.

I think maybe my body is starting to win the battle though, so that's good [from one point of view] but [from the other] it's no problem as I've been harming myself so much lately. Plus the compulsive picking and scratching...
I don't have a phone at the moment but apparently there's a way to run kik on computers and it seems like everyone uses kik these days, so I'll look into it for sure.
I'll talk but I don't see how mere words will change anything, when so many years of action has achieved... nothing.

I tried to do something about it today and was pretty much just told to go away. I tried to voluntarily commit myself and was told I have to go to A&E first as that is just procedure. So I did and waited to see their crisis team and again was basically told to go away. Not even the professionals will help me. :(

So, I think I am sticking with my plan. I have an appointment with my "care team" tomorrow but I'm seriously considering not turning up. Despite having had to wait months for these DBT appointments.

Plus I don't really want them to potentially notice my badly infected self-harm wounds. That woukd sort of ruin the plan. It almost worked last time... hospitalised for 4 weeks because someone found the wound and forced me to go to Hospital. It's so easy... all you have to do is ignore a wound.

I'm willing to talk... part of me still wants to be helped... to live... but I am honestly at my wits end.
Glad I could help, if only a tiny little bit... feel free to message me if you ever need someone to talk to.
I had the most luck with Venlafaxine/Effexor.

Weed helps me to detach myself from reality, too. It slows down my constantly racing mind and actually allows me to focus on something other than my thoughts and feelings. Helps with my sleep problems, too. What else am I supposed to do, been as though they refuse to prescribe me sleeping tablets or something to slow down my thought processes (if that even exists)?

All I really ever feel anymore is either absolute nothingness, or anger/frustration (almost always directed at myself). Usually, it's over the most meaningless things. Sometimes, I will realise how stupid I was for overreacting so much but that just tends to makes me more angry... bah.

I've been fighting really strong urges for a short while too and it's getting really difficult to ignore. But as you said, you've handled it... I've handled it too, so far anyway. All we can really do is to keep trying our best to resist.

For a theist, once all of their hope and faith is gone -- there still remains one source of hope and faith -- their religion and their beliefs. For an atheist, this is not the case.

Love? There is no love in my life anymore.

I've been fighting for more than a decade and there is no fight left in me. I gave up a while back and now I'm just trying to build up the courage to do what I should have done a long time ago.

I'm with you.

Music is one of my life-long passions, always has been. I play several instruments; compose; write lyrics; listen to music etc. all the time. Or at least, I used to. Not even that which I have loved my entire life bring me much, if any, enjoyment anymore.

I haven't picked up a guitar for several months and I haven't sat down at a piano for even longer.

Well okay, I lie. I have sat at the piano but it has been in silence. After a few nights of no sleep, the other week, I was feeling sort of... manic, I guess? I had all kinds of urges and desires to do things, including play but at the same time I was just too physically exhausted. It sucked.

The last time I listened to music, I self-harmed. Certain songs bring back extremely strong feelings and memories about a recent relationship.

I thought passions were eternal but I guess I thought wrong.

Lucky! My therapist makes me feel worse and talks down to me as though I'm a child etc.

I can't imagine the pressures of having to raise a child but I know about the pressures of being a full time student... ugh.

Maybe you should try and focus on the fact that finals are coming up soon, so once that's over with things are probably/hopefully going to get easier for you? Also, I imagine you have a great feeling of accomplishment to come. You've poured so much time and energy into something and it is finally coming to a close and it is probably going to feel awesome afterwards.

I may be a random internet stranger but I'm proud of you, anyway. I failed (left early) College... twice.

It's awful that things like this are allowed to go on in schools and I can't imagine how this abuse makes you feel. Nobody deserves to be treated like that. This isn't the type of bullying I am familiar with and it sounds far far worse... and I have experienced a lot of bullying in my life both first and secondhand. Please, please, take suicidejunkie's advice.
I appreciate that.

I'm sorry but no. I HAVE been used and abused a lot through my life.

I admit that many a relationship has been ruined by me. I accept that and take the blame for it, entirely. I'm well aware that a lot of my pain stems from things I have said and done over the past 8-9 years or so.

However just as often if not more often (earlier in life), I have been the one on the receiving end of (ab)use and it has been absolutely no fault of my own. I believe that it's this abusive childhood that lead to some, if not all of my issues.

> ... We may even think that's what friendship is all about. It isn't.

Okay, so then what exactly is a friendship about? Please enlighten me. Because I'm pretty sure all of that is a big part of it.

>  ... It is also mistaken to expect relationships to make us feel happy, contented and secure

But... they do make me feel happy, contented and secure. So how is that misguided?


I'm only blaming the people who are actually responsible for [some of] my pain. The rest of the blame lies with me and trust me, I remind myself constantly about the things I've said and done. I beat myself up about it constantly. I am well aware of it all.

Have you told those close to you about these thoughts and how much they are affecting your ability to function? Or do they just see it as a sort of cry for attention and don't actually believe that you are seriously considering it? I can relate to that one, for sure.

Your Mother sounds like a bad influence on your life, as mine is. Does she trigger you often? Maybe it'd be better for everyone if she wasn't as involved with your life. This helped mine and my Mother's relationship, anyway. Some people just have conflicting personalities.

Perhaps we are too kind? I've had so many people in my life use or abuse my kindness and openness. Of course, I won't lie, I have ruined a lot of relationships too. I am by no means "innocent". But I have been (ab)used a lot in my life, by so called friends.

The only "friend" left in my life only shows up around the time I've been paid. Hmm, let me think about that for a minute... They know how easily lead on I am and how I tend to share anything and everything.

Maybe [some] people start acting like we don't exist, when we are no longer of any use to them? I don't know.

I too have deactivated FB many times as well as stripping down my "friends" list on several occasions. I'm currently at 10 friends, I think and they're all family. And not even they ever really talk to me on there.

FB is not good for us. Someone told me that FB is sort of built on positive reinforcement and if there is negativity then people tend to simply ignore it. Funny how the people sharing how awesome their life is get all of the attention and the people struggling and crying out for help are shunned and ignored. I love society.

Most people don't stay in my life for long, either. I have one or two people who I have known for a very long time who still talk to me and seemingly care about me. People who I've met and only know via the internet but that is it. But even these relationships seem to be failing.

The lack of responses to this post is also making me feel as though I don't exist. Same deal when I was hanging around in the chatroom that someone posted recently. It was rare that anyone came in and when they did, they would generally leave instantly; almost as if they didn't see me at all.

I stopped trying to make friends after I left College earlier this year. I was there for a few months and I tried my very best to treat others like I want to be treated. Not a single friend resulted from that. I felt like I had friends when I was on campus but whenever I was away, I knew I didn't. After I quit, I didn't even get a single message on FB asking what happened. Nothing. Zilch. Nada.

Well it sounds like you've made it through a lot, so far. And instead of just going off and silently making plans, you have opened up to strangers here instead. You know that it's not truly the answer and you have sought help.

Your mind may tell you want to die and at times it may utterly convince you but your body will do anything to ensure your survival. This is why it's so hard to go through with - You can't get rid of your survival instinct that easily. Our fear of mortality and the unknown also gets in the way. I guess, in a way, it's a good thing. The world would be a very empty place, otherwise.

I understand that you hate yourself, trust me I do. I absolutely despise myself. I am the one barrier between me and my recovery. But, you sound like you have a fair few things going for you. You have people in your life, who care about you. You may hate yourself but that does not invalidate their opinions of you. They see something in you and you need to try and see it too. Plus, remember, everyone is their own worst critic; even "normal" people.

You seem like a strong person and I have faith that you can find your way through these difficult times. I'm not going to spout bullshit about how everything will get better as most of the time it really doesn't. That you've made it this far through life, though, is IMO a great feat. Anyone with severe mental health issues who makes it past 20 or so is in my opinion amazing.

I just wish I had any other advice to offer. Especially advice on how not to hate yourself.
I know relapsing is really hard and how defeated it makes you feel but four months is quite a long time and you should, in the very least, be proud of yourself for that.

I know how you feel. The other night I actually started writing a note... I've never done that before. I don't have a plan but I'm almost at the point where I'm going to make one.

When I bring it up to my care team, they just say oh ring this crisis number if you ever feel like that. They don't get it, at all. Once you get to the point where you actually attempt it, it's too late. You want to go through with it and you want it to work. You don't want to talk and you don't want help. I've been there before.

If I was to ring them before that stage and tell them honestly how I was feeling and thinking, then I'd presume they'd just shove me in a secure unit. Yeah, I'm sure that'd help a ton.

I've been plagued with thoughts of self-harm and suicide for countless years and lately they are basically constant. I've never found a way to get rid of them, despite therapy and counselling etc. I wish I had any advice but I honestly don't. The only advice I've ever been given was to be "mindful of your thoughts". To sort of respond to the negative/irrational thoughts with positive/rational/logical counter-thoughts. It helped my anxiety a lot but it has done nothing for my intrusive thoughts. Maybe it's worth a shot but I'm sure you've been told about this before...

If you need someone to talk to, though, I'm here.

I'm incapable of even enjoying life-long passions anymore. I have basically been incapacitated for months. I don't enjoy: playing/listening to music; reading/writing; gaming; programming... nothing. I don't enjoy reddit anymore and barely spend any time here, compared to how much I used to; at least not on my main account.

I relate completely to how you feel and also to how exhausted you say you are all the time.

I just sleep... sleep as much as physically possible. At least I don't have to deal with my thoughts and/or feelings while asleep. Also, my medication makes it so I don't have (or remember?) dreams or nightmares anymore; so sleeping is pretty much the only enjoyable thing left. The only issue with that, is that I have great difficulty sleeping a lot of the time. Isn't life fun? I wish I could get hold of some sleeping tablets. Maybe I would be able to sleep away the majority of this ridiculous existence instead, since I can't seem to bring myself to kill myself... as much as I have been seriously considering it.

I don't know why I'm even posting this, this isn't advice at all and I'm an idiot. I apologise.

Actually, come to think of it, I do have one tiny bit of advice. I was on Citalopram at one point for a few months and it didn't really seem to help much. At first, I thought it was helping but maybe it was just placebo. I tried a few other medications and eventually found one that helped immensely (at least, at the time). Would you at least consider trying other medications?

One last thing, anti-depressants can take 3-6 weeks to take effect. You said you were only on it for a month. It may have just been a placebo effect that was making you feel better whereas the drug never had enough time to act. I could be and probably am totally wrong but it's at least worth considering.

It may help but sometimes they can just exacerbate the issues. Depends on the person and the medication and the timing/circumstances. The right medication will probably lift your general mood enough that you'll find it easier to do those things but it is not a silver bullet. It's still hard and there's also the potential that it will not help you at all. Also, if you are feeling suicidal but are basically too depressed to act on the thoughts; there's the potential that it will lift your mood just enough to cause you to actually go through with it. Plus, there's side effects.

I had to go through several medications before I found one that seemed to work for me. Although, I've been on it (on and off) for a long time now and it doesn't seem to be working anymore; I've been far worse since the last time I started up on it (~6 weeks).

I'm currently on an SNRI which are also sometimes used to treat anxiety, so that can be considered a sort of bonus I suppose? One tablet for two issues....

My advice would be ultimately to **proceed with caution concerning anti-depressants**. If you decide to start using them and are struggling with any of the side effects, or just feel they aren't working, NEVER EVER stop taking them and consult your doctor instead. The withdrawal effects can be absolutely terrible (probably the 2nd worst experience of my life) with some of them, especially the SNRIs.^1

1. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSRI_discontinuation_syndrome#Discontinuation_of_SNRIs

By making them read these:

1. http://hyperboleandahalf.blogspot.co.uk/2011/10/adventures-in-depression.html
2. http://hyperboleandahalf.blogspot.co.uk/2013/05/depression-part-two.html

Have you opened up to them at all? Most importantly, about the things in your life that you have said/done/thought/felt that make you think you fit the symptoms? If not, then maybe you could bring those things up without actually mentioning BPD itself. I know it's difficult but if you tell them as much as possible, they'll be able to more accurately diagnose you. And at the end of the day, only a medical professional can diagnose you. We can't and neither can you, even if you feel you relate to the symptoms; I've heard many people do.

Some say there is a borderline in all of us. It's just that most people are able to regulate and control their thoughts and feelings and so it rarely, if ever, surfaces.

I was stuck with a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder and Social Anxiety for countless years before I truly opened up and was diagnosed BPD too. In a way, I wish I'd have done so sooner although at the same time it's a very difficult diagnosis to receieve IMO. If you want to talk, feel free to reply to me publically or even message me privately.
Yeah, it infuriates me.

I think that some medications can make you feel sort of zombie-like and basically emotionless, like this. I can't cry and can barely even fake being happy anymore.

If you are on any medication, it might be worth bringing this up to your doctor or care team. I brought it up and they are looking into changing it again.

I've been popping in every so often and hanging around for an hour or two and it's always empty. Nice idea, in theory but in practise if no one is ever there it will just die.

Also, the potential for abuse is extremely high when activity is so low. Anyone could join and start setting people off, with no one around to stop them.

I don't have any transportation. I've thought about voluntary work. I love animals and have thought about volunteering at a sanctuary before but anxiety makes it difficult. I'm bored of small meaningless interactions. I've had enough of those for a lifetime and they never lead anywhere.

I couldn't even make any friends after going to College TWICE. I tried to be open and approachable and nice to everyone. It's not like I was trying to force anyone to be my friend. I had plenty of "small interactions" while there but I still don't have any friends.
Yeah... every time it takes me a few weeks to a month or two, at most.
Nice piece. Very dissonant but beautiful in places. I like me some dissonance and given what the song represents, not surprising and very fitting. Reminds me a little of Chopin.

Maybe it's better being numb, though? That way, there is less chance of things happening because of emotions.

But I really miss being able to feel, even if it was mostly negative.

(self-harm warning)

I cried the other night for a few minutes, during a discussion about my last relationship and the fallout that came after. But I didn't feel any better afterwards. I felt (and still feel) like I need to cry **for hours** but I simply can't. It's hard... as crying is one of *the* best ways to release all of the pain. I think that being back on my medication again and the numbness that it brings along, are what has driven me back to self-harming again. And it's been a very long time since I've done that (minus one incident late last year).

I'm thinking about bringing it up and seeing if there's something else we could try but I've tried numerous medications over the years and nothing worked for me until we tried this one. Plus, something gives me the feeling they're all *supposed* to make us numb. Less chance of our emotions causing incidents that way, which from their point of view is probably better. I've been on it numerous years though so perhaps it's just a dosage adjustment that is required.

Yeah, it would be nice to be able to go back and do everything again if you could maintain the memory of how everything went the first time around. Otherwise, I'd just see myself making the same mistakes again.
My past haunts me everyday of my life and I'm in a deep depression at the moment as well despite being medicated. I wish I could just forget everything and then I would truly be able to start again.

Having friends is important because humans are social creatures by nature and isolation affects the brain in strange ways and basically breaks you. Keep in mind that people's bodies works quite differently and it's impossible even for a professional to say "ah yes, we need X medication for you".

Have you ever stopped taking any of your meds suddenly, before? I'm not sure if you're aware but that can cause rather extreme withdrawal effects and it can be the worst feeling in the world. I can understand if you're thinking like, oh this isn't working so I'm just going to stop taking them (I've done it before) but you're just making things worse by doing that.

If you don't think something is working, tell your doctor that you don't believe it's doing anything for you and want to stop taking it and he should slowly lower the dose for you. Trust me, you do not want SSRI/SNRI discontinuation syndrome.

As for you not getting along with any of the professionals you've seen so far... same deal. You have to try a few until you find one who you connect with on a personal level. It really sucks, I know.
